title: SNAP work requirements increase procedural denials through administrative burden
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34698, administrative SNAP data analyzed with age-based exemption and waiver-period difference-in-differences designs
geography: United States SNAP administrative-policy setting; study-selected jurisdictions and Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs), not a national participation rate

observations.period: 2026 NBER Working Paper 34698; study-defined waiver and work-requirement periods

denominator.unit: SNAP administrative records for study-selected jurisdictions and ABAWD age-exemption comparisons; exact public abstract denominator is not disclosed

procedural_denials.value: Work requirements significantly increase procedural denials

overall_denials.value: Work requirements significantly increase overall denials

participation_deterrence.value: The results indicate that work requirements deter participation through imposed administrative burdens

comparison_design.value: Age-based exemptions for people aged 50 and older and waiver periods provide the identifying comparisons

observations.method: Administrative-data study using difference-in-differences models that exploit age-based exemptions applying to ABAWDs aged 50 and older and periods in which work-requirement waivers apply.
observations.uncertainty: The public abstract does not disclose the full administrative-record denominator, selected jurisdictions, effect magnitudes, or every implementation detail. The design identifies policy-associated denial changes under its assumptions; it does not show individual intent, notice receipt, administrative effort, appeal, benefit restoration, food security, health, work quality, or later political action.
observations.subgroup: SNAP ABAWDs around the study's age-exemption boundary, waiver versus work-requirement periods, and study-selected administrative jurisdictions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Denial changes could reflect concurrent policy, labor-market, or administrative changes if the identifying assumptions fail. A procedural denial may represent incomplete paperwork, failure to document an exemption, or another process route rather than a final loss of eligibility; deterrence is a mechanism interpretation, not proof of every claimant's reason for nonparticipation.

related_sources.claim: Related NBER SNAP work-requirement participation and labor-supply study; not pooled with this procedural-denial design.

boundary: This record adds a policy-to-administrative-denial and participation-deterrence mechanism. It does not establish a national denial rate, individual notice or effort, appeal, restored benefits, food security, health, durable hardship, trust, or political action.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official NBER landing-page HTML and abstract reviewed; the underlying administrative data are not retained.
